title: Ranking Every Ocarina of Time Dungeon (Worst to Best)
creator: Nate Plays
description:
All eight main dungeons in Ocarina of Time, ranked. Fight me in the comments.

This video is sponsored by Raycon. Get 15% off at https://raycon.com/nate

What's your #1? Wrong answers only.

sentences.t: Okay, today we're ranking every main dungeon in Ocarina of Time from worst to best, and some of you are going to be very upset.
Quick ground rules, I'm only counting the eight main dungeons, so no Bottom of the Well, no Ice Cavern, and no Ganon's Castle.
Starting at the bottom, number eight, Jabu-Jabu's Belly.
You spend the whole dungeon carrying Princess Ruto around like a sack of potatoes, and she complains the entire time.
The visuals are gross in a fun way, but the layout is just confusing, and the boss is forgettable.
Number seven, the Water Temple.
I know, I know, everyone expects it at the bottom.
But honestly, once you understand the three water levels, it's a really clever design, it's just punishing if you miss one key.
The iron boots menuing is what kills it, and the 3DS version fixed most of that.
Number six, Dodongo's Cavern.
It's the second dungeon, so it's short, but blowing up walls with bomb flowers is so satisfying.
And King Dodongo eating bombs is one of the most iconic boss fights in the series.
Number five, the Fire Temple.
Great music, or at least the original version with the chanting, before they changed it.
And the climb up the tower at the end is a lot of fun.
Number four, the Great Deku Tree.
It's a tutorial, but it's a perfect tutorial, it teaches you everything without saying a word.
Okay, before the top three, this video is sponsored by Ray Con.

That's ray con dot com slash nate.
Alright, number three, the Forest Temple.
This is where Ocarina goes from a kid's adventure to something actually creepy.
The twisted hallways, the four Poe sisters, Phantom Ganon riding out of the paintings.
The only thing keeping it from number one is the block puzzles, which go on a little long.
Number two, the Spirit Temple.
You play it as young Link and adult Link, and the way the two halves connect is genius.
Plus Twinrova is a great boss, you're bouncing their fire and ice back at each other with the mirror shield.
And number one.
It's the Water Temple.
No, I'm kidding, put the pitchfork down.
Number one is the Shadow Temple.
Invisible walls, guillotines, a boat ride across a river of the dead, and the Lens of Truth actually matters for once.
It was the darkest thing Nintendo had made at that point, and it still holds up.
Bongo Bongo is a weird boss, but the drum music in that room lives in my head rent-free.
So that's my list.
Tell me which one I got completely wrong in the comments, and I'll see you in the next one.
